description:
Mesh non-orthogonality in the cfmesh pipeline traces to the TET PRIMAL, not to the dual operation or the solver. Fix the tet mesher.

EVIDENCE THAT THE DUAL IS EXACT (measured 2026-08-07, test re-run and passing):
crates/outram-foam-mesh/tests/poly_dual_mesh.rs:212 dual_quality_is_exactly_orthogonal_on_a_uniform_block asserts max_non_ortho_deg < 1e-12, mean < 1e-12, max_skewness < 1e-12 (:226-232). Re-ran `cargo test -p outram-foam-mesh --release --test poly_dual_mesh`: 3^3 block -> 64 dual cells, non-orthogonality max 0.000 deg / mean 0.000 deg, skewness 0.0000, verdict GOOD; 4^3 block identical. The metric itself is closed-form validated in crates/outram-foam-mesh/src/mesh_quality.rs:600 (Cartesian block = 0) and :651 (sheared block matches atan(k) at 45/60/86 deg to 1e-10).

IMPORTANT CORRECTION -- that test is NOT of cfmesh's dual. It exercises outram_foam_mesh::poly_dual_mesh, the CELL-CENTRE polyDualMesh (poly_dual_mesh.rs:25-41). cfmesh uses a DIFFERENT algorithm, the median/Donald vertex-centred dual (crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/dual.rs:48-70, which says so explicitly). cfmesh's four dual tests (dual.rs:441, :474, :499, :543) check only closure, volume conservation, boundary match and face count. So "the dual is exact" is MEASURED for outram-foam-mesh's dual and only INFERRED for cfmesh's.
=> First sub-task: add an orthogonality test for cfmesh's own median dual on a uniform block. Until that exists the diagnosis is one step short of proven.

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT THE TET PRIMAL:
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/tet.rs:93 pub fn tetrahedralize(mesh: &VolumeMesh) -- centroid subdivision (every cell -> cell.face.edge tets). Its two tests (tet.rs:169, :197) assert ONLY positive volume, closedness, boundary area = 6, volume = 1, 4 triangular faces per cell. No non-orthogonality or skewness metric is asserted on the tet primal anywhere in the tree.
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/delaunay.rs:42-44 states the defect qualitatively: centroid subdivision "is not a Delaunay one -- some interior faces fail the empty-circumsphere (locally-Delaunay) test, which is what leaves slivers."
- crates/outram-park-fork-cfmesh/src/pipeline.rs:774-775 records uniform 0.40 m -> max non-orth 85.14 deg and uniform 0.30 m -> 85.38 deg, and :804-805 notes those runs "report polyhedral dual skipped -- their output is the tetrahedralization". Dualised rows at the same geometry measure 71.7-72.5 deg. This supports the direction of the claim.
  CAVEAT: those ~85 deg figures are DOC-RECORDED, not test-asserted. The test at pipeline.rs:812 runs only two of the eight table rows and asserts merely max_non_orthogonality_deg < 90.0 (:842). Do not cite 85.14/85.38 as measured-by-CI.

WORK:
1. Add an orthogonality/skewness test for cfmesh's median dual on a uniform block (close the inference gap above).
2. Add non-orthogonality + skewness metrics to the tet primal tests in tet.rs.
3. Replace or repair centroid subdivision with a locally-Delaunay tetrahedralization (see delaunay.rs) so slivers are removed at source.

NOTED TENSION: the same fleet added a solver-side non-orthogonal correction -- crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_operators/fvm/laplacian_corrected.rs (untracked) and crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/tests/non_orthogonal_laplacian.rs. So "do not chase a solver-side correction" is an editorial recommendation the tree currently contradicts. The maintainer should decide whether that correction stays (it is legitimate OpenFOAM practice regardless) -- the point of this bead is that it must not be treated as a SUBSTITUTE for fixing the tet mesher.
title: cfmesh: fix tet-primal mesh quality — it is the real non-orthogonality source, not the dual

description:
FOUND 2026-08-14 while doing op-6tz.35.1 (TRISO shell S(alpha,beta) wiring). Confirmed from the decks themselves, not inferred.

SYMPTOM. Regenerating tsl-CinSiC (MAT 44) and tsl-SiinSiC (MAT 43) from their embedded decks via leapr::generate::generate_tape with ElasticChannel::Generate yields laws with elastic_xs identically 0.0. Measured at 0.0253 eV, barn per principal atom:
  C in graphite : elastic 4.55555 + inelastic 0.48162 = 5.03717   (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> bound 5.0372, +2.01%)
  C in SiC      : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.13291 = 0.13291   (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> bound 0.1329, -97.31%)
  Si in SiC     : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.06367 = 0.06367   (free-gas Si28 1.9914 -> bound 0.0637, -96.80%)

A bound crystalline solid scattering 97% LESS than the free gas it replaces is not physical. It is exactly the failure mode op-nhoa named for graphite -- an inelastic-only law missing its dominant elastic channel -- so a caller who wired this in would give the SiC layer ~2.7% of its true thermal scattering and get a plausible wrong k, not a crash.

ROOT CAUSE, from the deck files in crates/njoy-outram-park-fork/src/leapr/decks/:
  1. Card 4 (awr spr npr iel ncold): tsl-crystalline-graphite has iel=1 (NJOY built-in graphite lattice); tsl-CinSiC and tsl-SiinSiC have iel=0, i.e. NO built-in lattice, so stock LEAPR emits no coherent-elastic section.
  2. Both SiC decks' own comment cards state that 'modifications to the LEAPR source code were made to calculate the coherent elastic', citing Y. Zhu and A. Hawari, 'Implementation of a Generalized Coherent Elastic Scattering Formulation for Thermal Neutron Scattering'.

So this is NOT a defect in this workspace's LEAPR port. The port faithfully reproduces stock NJOY LEAPR, which carries built-in lattices only for graphite / Be / BeO and cannot produce a general crystal structure factor. It is a capability gap.

OPTIONS, in rough order of cost:
  (a) Obtain the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-CinSiC / tsl-SiinSiC TAPES rather than regenerating from decks. The tapes carry the evaluator's coherent-elastic MF=7/MT=2 already, so ThermalScattering::from_endf_file would pick it up with no new physics. Cheapest by far. Note this reintroduces an external-data dependency the embedded decks removed, so it likely wants the acquire/cache path (op-6tz.28) rather than a hardcoded path.
  (b) Implement the generalized coherent-elastic formulation (Zhu and Hawari) in the LEAPR port -- a general structure factor from lattice parameters instead of the three hardcoded lattices. Correct and reusable for every non-built-in crystalline scatterer, but real work and needs its own V&V.
  (c) Leave the SiC layer free-gas and DOCUMENT it as a known modelling limitation. Currently the honest default, and what the code says today.

DO NOT substitute the graphite law for the SiC layer. Carbon bound in silicon carbide is a different lattice from carbon bound in graphite; the two laws are measurably different (97.36% apart at 0.0253 eV, though that figure is inflated by this very gap).

CURRENT STATE IN TREE. tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs asserts this gap deliberately -- sic_carbon_elastic_channel_is_missing_from_the_embedded_deck and sic_silicon_elastic_channel_is_missing_from_the_embedded_deck assert elastic == 0.0, so if the capability lands they FAIL and force the docs and this bead to be updated rather than letting inelastic-only data stay silently in use. geometry/triso_particle.rs's module doc records the limitation where a reader meets it.

Blocks a physically correct TRISO shell-resolved thermal transport case (op-6tz.35).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-08-17: option (a) is now available and MEASURED. The maintainer committed the official ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-CinSiC tape (MAT 44, 7.2 MB, commit ffef0fb76f); it now lives at reference-data/endf/tsl-CinSiC.endf after op-mixd moved tapes out of crates/.

The tape carries MF=7/MT=2 LTHR=1: 685 Bragg edges over 8 temperatures. Read through the existing SabSource::EndfTape path (no new physics needed), measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:

  C in SiC, regenerated from deck : elastic 0.00000 + inelastic 0.13291 = 0.13291  (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> -97.3%)
  C in SiC, from the committed tape: elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.13880 = 3.07957  (free-gas C0 4.9382 -> -37.6%)
  C in graphite, for scale         : elastic 4.55142 + inelastic 0.48634 = 5.03776
  Bragg cutoff, C in SiC: 1.066463e-3 eV (graphite: 1.822327e-3 eV)

So the tape gives 23x the total thermal cross section the deck path gives, and the -37.6% bound-vs-free figure is physically plausible where -97.3% was not.

NOT YET DONE, so this bead stays open:
  - The two GAP tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs still assert elastic == 0.0. They are designed to fail when the gap closes; they have not been flipped, because nothing yet routes the SiC layer at the tape.
  - tsl-SiinSiC.endf (MAT 43) was NOT committed -- only CinSiC plus three graphite grades. The silicon half of the SiC layer is still inelastic-only. Maintainer says they will upload it.
  - geometry/triso_particle.rs module doc still records the limitation.

MAINTAINER DIRECTION 2026-08-17: option (b) -- implement the Zhu and Hawari generalized coherent-elastic formulation in coher.rs -- was chosen over wiring the tape alone, so the capability is wanted regardless. Prerequisite: neither Zhu 2014 (MS thesis, NCSU) nor Zhu and Hawari 2015 (ICNC) is in crates/kovan-literature; per the workspace literature HARD RULE they must be catalogued before their formulation is used. The committed tsl-CinSiC MT=2 (685 edges, 8 temperatures) is then a real published oracle to validate the implementation against, and reproducing the six built-in NJOY lattices through the general path is a second free gate.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-08-17 (2): the silicon half is now supplied too (op-84v6). Both SiC tapes live in reference-data/endf/. Measured at 0.0253 eV / 296 K, barn per principal atom:

  C in SiC  (MAT 44): elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.13880 = 3.07957  (free-gas C 4.9382 -> -37.6%)
  Si in SiC (MAT 43): elastic 2.94078 + inelastic 0.06615 = 3.00693  (free-gas Si-28 1.9914 -> +51.0%)

CRITICAL for wiring: those two elastic figures are identical because MAT 43 and MAT 44 carry byte-identical MF=7/MT=2 sections (1044 records each; only the header ZA/AWR differs). Coherent elastic is a lattice property of 3C-SiC, not a per-sublattice one. So summing the elastic channels of both materials double-counts Bragg scattering -- MT=2 must be attributed to the compound once. This is a real trap: it would give a plausible wrong k rather than a crash, the same failure mode this bead was opened about.

Also: the evaluator's tsl-SiinSiC.readme (shipped with the tape, now in reference-data/endf/) states in its own words that the coherent elastic 'was generated using an in-house routine [1]', citing Zhu and Hawari, ICNC 2015. That is independent corroboration of this bead's root-cause analysis, from the evaluation itself rather than inferred from card 4's iel=0.

Still open, unchanged: the two GAP tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs still assert elastic == 0.0 (they test the DECK path, which remains correctly elastic-free); nothing yet routes the SiC layer at the tapes; and the maintainer's chosen path is option (b), implementing the Zhu-Hawari generalized formulation, for which the two papers are still not in kovan-literature.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
2026-08-21 -- the "Si in SiC inelastic is 3.7% short" figure recorded in this
bead is RETRACTED as an artefact. It was a temperature mismatch, not physics.

The deck was regenerated at 293.6 K (outram-mc-libs' TEMPERATURE_K) and
compared against a tape read at 296 K, which NJOY's T/1000+5 = 5.296 K match
tolerance snaps to the tape's 300 K block. Two different temperatures.

Measured like-for-like (commit 1a904fc5), sigma at 0.0253 eV, b/atom:
  deck @ 293.6 K : inelastic 0.063673
  deck @ 300   K : inelastic 0.066150
  tape @ 300   K : inelastic 0.066150   <- 0.0000% difference
The whole -3.74% was the 6.4 K gap.

Stronger statement, now committed as
tests/leapr_temperature_block_selection.rs::
si_in_sic_kernel_reproduces_the_published_evaluation_at_every_temperature:
regenerating S(alpha,beta) from tsl-SiinSiC.leapr reproduces
reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.endf at ALL 8 declared temperatures --
306,033 tabulated points, worst deviation 0.0000% (ENDF's 6-digit write
precision), T_eff exact at every temperature. The Si-in-SiC INELASTIC kernel
is validated against the published evaluation.

What remains open in this bead is only the ELASTIC side: deck-regenerated
coherent elastic is 2.85169 b at 300 K against the tape's 2.94078 b, -3.03%.
That is the residual from the generalized coherent-elastic implementation
(op-jw4a) and is tracked in op-4daf, not here.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
CLOSING 2026-08-21. The capability gap this bead names is closed.

The symptom was elastic_xs identically 0.0 for both SiC materials, i.e. a
bound crystalline solid scattering 97% LESS than the free gas it replaces.
Option (b) -- implement the Zhu & Hawari generalized coherent-elastic
formulation -- was the maintainer's choice (2026-08-17) and is implemented
(op-jw4a, commit 8933cdbf).

Measured now, 0.0253 eV / 300 K, b per principal atom, like-for-like against
reference-data/endf/tsl-SiinSiC.endf:
  elastic    2.85169  vs tape 2.94078   (-3.03%)   -- was 0.00000
  inelastic  0.066150 vs tape 0.066150  (+0.0000%)

and the earlier "-3.7% inelastic" figure in this bead is retracted as a
temperature artefact (see the previous comment).

Both "do not work around it" warnings this bead raised still stand and are
recorded where a reader meets them (outram-mc-libs/src/geometry/
triso_particle.rs module doc): do not substitute the graphite law for SiC, and
do not sum both SiC materials' elastic channels for one region -- they carry
the identical compound structure factor by design, so summing double-counts
Bragg scattering. The second is pinned by a test.

REMAINING, tracked in op-4daf (not lost by this close): the -3.03% elastic
residual, the edge-by-edge MT=2 comparison, and rewriting the two #[ignore]d
gap tests in outram-mc-libs/tests/triso_shell_thermal_scattering.rs to real
tolerance-based assertions.

Note for op-6tz.35, which this blocked: the SiC layer is now modellable, but
with a stated ~3% elastic bias. Whether that is good enough for a shell-
resolved TRISO transport case is a judgement call for whoever picks it up --
it is no longer a 97% error, and it is no longer zero.

title: njoy LEAPR: no SiC coherent-elastic -- stock LEAPR cannot generate it, so the TRISO SiC layer has no usable S(alpha,beta)

description:
Maintainer, 2026-08-04: 'we should have a standard HP and LP turbine as it is for the PWR plants' -- in the widget library.

CORRECTION THIS CARRIES. On 2026-08-04 the mirrored 'hourglass' silhouette inherited from fhr_sim_v2 was called an artwork defect and replaced with monotonic inlet-to-exhaust blade growth (commit b44f549). That was only half right. A PWR LP turbine is normally DOUBLE-FLOW: steam admits at the centre and expands outward in BOTH directions, so its rotor genuinely is mirrored about the mid-plane. The real defect was applying one silhouette unconditionally, plus proportions that collapsed at wide aspect ratios. Flow path is a property of the machine, not a drawing style.

WHAT TO BUILD:
  - Single-flow: monotonic expansion, inlet one end, exhaust the other. Typical HP.
  - Double-flow: centre admission, mirrored expansion to an exhaust at each end. Typical PWR LP, and how the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork was actually shaped.

Closed set -> enum dispatch, per the workspace no-trait-objects rule.

STANDARD PWR SECONDARY ARRANGEMENT to represent:
  - Steam generators deliver SATURATED (not superheated) steam, roughly 6-7 MPa.
  - HP turbine expands to roughly 1 MPa. Wet steam throughout, so erosion matters.
  - A moisture separator reheater (MSR) sits between HP and LP -- it is a distinct component and is NOT currently in the widget library at all. Worth its own bead.
  - Typically two or three double-flow LP turbines exhaust to the condenser at vacuum (~5 kPa).
  - LP last-stage blades are very long; the annulus area ratio between HP and LP is large and should be visible when the two widgets are shown side by side.

RELATION TO OTHER BEADS: per-stage blade angulation and the impulse/reaction mix are op-wqk.14.11 (placeholders now, real angles when the physical turbine model lands, op-dt3.18). Physical envelope dimensions remain blocked on op-dt3.17.1. This bead is about the FLOW PATH and the HP/LP presets, which are independent of both.

DO NOT present the presets as a specific vendor's or plant's design -- they are illustrative standard-arrangement values per RESPONSIBLE_USE.md, and the data policy forbids using any actual plant data.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
DECIDED 2026-08-04 (maintainer): DOUBLE-FLOW IS THE DEFAULT for turbine widgets. Single-flow remains available as the other enum variant, but a TurbineVisual built without specifying a flow path draws double-flow.

This matches large-PWR practice rather than being merely a drawing preference: at PWR secondary-side volumetric flows, the HP turbine is commonly double-flow as well as the LP set (a typical large PWR turbine-generator is one double-flow HP plus two or three double-flow LP cylinders). So double-flow is the right default for BOTH presets, not just LP.

Practical consequence for the implementation: the mirrored silhouette from the original fhr_sim_v2 artwork becomes the DEFAULT rendering again, with centre admission and an exhaust at each end -- but now with the pitch-derived proportions from b44f549 so it no longer collapses at wide aspect ratios, and with the blade-height growth running outward from the centre admission plane toward both exhausts (not inward, and not mirrored-by-accident as before).

title: Widget library: standard PWR HP and LP turbines (single-flow vs double-flow)
